title: Normalized row cycles in the second graded filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $\mathcal B$ a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $I$ be a commuting bicomplex with complex degree in $\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree in $\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $R_s=F(I.X(s))$, $J=\operatorname{flip}(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(F)(I))$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and $K=\operatorname{Tot}(J)$. Let $L$ be a decreasing filtration of $K$ by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration] such that its degreewise steps equal the second filtration of $J$. Fix $r\in\mathbf N$, $s\in\mathbf Z$, and $n=s+r$. Write $a_{r,s}:R_s^r\to K^n$ for the inverse of the extension-by-zero isomorphism followed by the $(r,s)$ diagonal coprojection. Let $t:\operatorname{cycles}^r(R_s)\to (L^sK)^n$ satisfy $t m=i_{\mathrm{cycles}}a_{r,s}$, where $m$ is the filtration inclusion. Put $Z=L.\mathrm{complexCycles}(s,n,1)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and let $q:(L^sK)^n\to (\operatorname{gr}^s L)^n$ be the graded projection. There exists an isomorphism $c:\operatorname{cycles}^r(R_s)\cong Z$ such that $c\,\iota_Z=tq$. No boundary quotient or homology comparison is asserted.

proof.text: In degree n the step is the sum of images of diagonal inclusions with second coordinate in [s,n]. Project the total coproduct onto its (r,s) summand and apply the extension isomorphism. All summands of the next step have second coordinate at least s+1, so the projection kills that step and descends to the quotient. Lift the (r,s) inclusion through the step in the opposite direction. The composites are identity on the s summand, and all other generating summands vanish in the quotient, proving both inverse identities. This works for negative s and for r=0.

The total differential on each diagonal inclusion is the resolution differential plus the signed differential raising s. The second component factors through the next step and is killed by the graded projection. Thus the term comparisons commute with the outgoing resolution differential. Apply kernel universal properties to both inverse term maps; the first-page cycle formula identifies the graded kernel with Z. The filtration inclusion is mono, so the specified t equals the restriction of the term lift. The resulting cycle isomorphism therefore satisfies c.hom followed by the cycle inclusion = t followed by the graded projection. Zero rows have zero cycles and the same argument gives the unique zero-object isomorphism.

theorem secondFiltration_row_graded_cycles
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    (I : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (L : DecreasingFiltration
      ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).total
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hL : ∀ p n : ℤ, L.complexStep p n =
      ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).secondFiltration n).step
        p)
    (r : ℕ) (s : ℤ)
    (t : ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X s)).cycles r ⟶
      (L.step s : CochainComplex B ℤ).X (s + (r : ℤ)))
    (ht : t ≫ (L.step s).arrow.f (s + (r : ℤ)) =
      ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X s)).iCycles r ≫
      ((((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X s)).extendXIso
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (by rfl)).inv ≫
        (((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).ιTotal
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (r : ℤ) s (s + (r : ℤ)) (by
            change (r : ℤ) + s = s + (r : ℤ)
            omega))) :
    ∃ c : ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X s)).cycles r ≅
        (L.complexCycles s (s + (r : ℤ)) 1 : B),
      c.hom ≫ (L.complexCycles s (s + (r : ℤ)) 1).arrow =
        t ≫ (L.complexQuotientπ s (s + 1) (by omega)).f (s + (r : ℤ))
